title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Deregulatory and Other Measures) Bill 2015
short_title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Deregulatory and Other Measures) Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change competition and consumer law administration, removing some reporting and consent requirements while expanding court access and the regulator's enforcement options.
It would exempt food incidents from consumer product safety reporting and let private litigants pursue overseas breaches without first obtaining written ministerial consent.
Incidents caused by food packaging would remain reportable, and the amendments would begin on the day after royal assent, subject to their application provisions.
changes: State and territory courts would gain jurisdiction over pyramid selling and manufacturers' liability for unsafe goods.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission could seek court orders compelling compliance with information notices.
Traders could not supply unsolicited goods or services, or seek payment, before the cooling-off period begins.
Specified agencies could receive product safety notices where disclosure is reasonably necessary to protect public safety.
summary.affected: Businesses, consumers, private litigants, courts and the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission are affected.
